The Petitioners in M.V.C. No.1418/2021 and MVC.1673/2021 have filed the Petitions against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs. 15,00,000/
and Rs. 15,00,000/ respectively for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

sentences.text: 2. Since both these Petitions arises out of the same accident and in view of the Order dated 1502 2022 in MVC No.1418/2021, these two cases were clubbed together and taken for common disposal.

3. The substance of averments made in both the Petitions are as under:
That on 09032021 at about 3.45 p.m. the Petitioners were proceeding on a TVS Victor motor cycle bearing No.KA06HC8043 in front of Boregowda House,
Gandhamachanahalli, Honnudike Hand post to Honnudike road, Guluru Hobali,
Tumkuru District, at that time, a car bearing No.KA04MW6914 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the motor cycle of the Petitioners.
Due to the said impact, both Petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, Petitioner in MVC.1418/2021 was shifted to Hemavathi Hospital for first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital and later he was shifted to Hemavathi Hospital for further treatment.
Immediately after the accident, Petitioner in MVC.1673/2021 was shifted to Hemavathi Hospital for treatment.

4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner in MVC.1418/2021 was hale and healthy and he was working as an agriculturist and milk vendor and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
5.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner in MVC.No.1673/2021 was hale and healthy and working as tailor and was earning Rs.15,000/ per month.

Krishnaveni B.C vs Renukaiah P.H on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145936825/
2 6.

The Petitioners of both the Petitions have contended that the accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA04MW6914 which is owned by the Respondent No.1 and insured with Respondent No.2.
As such, both the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
7. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents in both petitions, the Respondent No.1 did not appear before the court and hence he was placed Exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed its detailed Objection Statement.
8. In both the petitions, Respondent No.2 has denied the age, avocation and the income of the Petitioners.
Further it denied that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Further it contended that the driver of the car was not possessing valid and effective driving license and the car had no valid permit and FC.

Further it contended that the owner of the car knowing fully that the driver did not possess valid driving licence has entrusted the said vehicle to him and has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioners in both the petitions and the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioners.
Further it contended that the rider of the Motorcycle did not possess valid driving license.
On these grounds, it has prayed to dismiss both the petitions.
9. On the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor in office has framed following Issues.
ISSUES IN MVC No.1418/2021 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 09.03.2021 at about 3.45 p.m. in front Boregowda Hosue, Gandhamachanahalli,
Honnudike Hand post to Honnudike road, Guluru Hobli, |Tumkuru District, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing No.KA04MW6914?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award ?
ISSUES IN MVC No.1673/2021 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 09.03.2021 at about 3.45 p.m. in front Boregowda Hosue, Gandhamachanahalli,
Honnudike Hand post to Honnudike road, Guluru Hobli, |Tumkuru District, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing No.KA04MW6914?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What Order or Award ?

sentences.text: In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner in MVC.1418/2021 got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P18, Ex. P.26 to 28.

The Petitioner in MVC.1673/2021 got examined herself as P.W.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P19 to Ex.P25 and examined two witnesses as PW.3 and PW.4 on their behalf and got marked documents as per Ex.P.27 to P33 and closed their side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 did not choose to adduce any evidence.
11. I have heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioners and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.
I have perused the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record.

12. My answer to the Issues in MVC.1418/2021 are as under :
 Issue No. 1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
15. In order to prove the case of the petitioners, Petitioners in both the cases have been examined as P.W.1 and PW.2 and they also examined two witnesses as P.W.3 and PW.4.
They got marked in total 33 documents.

Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 are the True copies of FIR along with Complaint, Spot Panchanama, Seizer Panchanama, Notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Reply to the Notice, IMV report,
Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet.

Ex.P2 is the Spot Panchanama which shows that the concerned police had drawn the Spot Panchanama at the spot in the presence of panchas.

17.
Ex.P.9 is the notarized copy of Aadhar card of the petitioner in MVC.1418/2021.
Ex.P10 and 11 are the Discharge summaries which shows that the Petitioner in MVC.1418/2021 was admitted as an inpatient on 09032021 and discharged on 1503 2021 and from 16.03.2021 to 18.03.2021.
Ex.P.12 is the Inpatient bill, Ex.P13 is the Medical Bills, Ex.P.14 is the Prescriptions, Ex.P.15 is the Photographs, Ex. P.16 is the CD.
Ex.P17 is the Medical reports, Ex.P.18 is the CT scan films, Ex. P.26 is the Account statement by Milk Federation, Ex.P.27 is the Notarised copy of driving licence and Ex. P.28 is the Medical bills.

Ex.P21 is the Discharge summary.

P.24 is the Photographs and Ex.P.25 is the Xrays.
19. Further, Petitioner in MVC.1418/2021 has examined medical record officer namely Shaik Moin as PW.3 and got marked two documents as per Ex.P.29 and 30 i.e., Authorisation letter and Case sheet.
He also examined Dr. Banu Prakash as P.W.4 and he got marked documents at Ex.P.31 to P.33 i.e., OPD card and Disability certificate and Neurobehavioral and cognitive assessment clinical data sheet.
20. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 has cross examined the P.W.1 and PW.2 at length.
In the crossexamination both PW.1 and PW.2 have denied the suggestions and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the Petitioners.

21. Though the Respondent No.2 had taken contention that the accident does not caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, it did not lead any evidence to substantiate its contentions.
Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Chargesheet against the driver of the offending car.

22. The oral and documentary evidence of P.W.1 and PW.2 and the materials available on record,
clearly shows that the said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and Petitioners in both the cases have sustained injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in both the cases in the "Affirmative".

23. Issue No. 2 in MVC.1418/2021 : As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

Krishnaveni B.C vs Renukaiah P.H on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145936825/
5 24.
In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 49 years.
The Petitioner has produced Aadhar card at Ex. P.9 to prove his age.
As per Aadhar card, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 22.03.1971.
The accident took place on 09.03.2021.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is 51 years which is to be taken for the purpose of assessment.
25. Further, the Petitioner has averred that he was doing agriculture and milk vending business and was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.26 document to substantiate the said fact.
Upon careful consideration of Ex. P.26, it is clear that the said document reflects the entries pertaining to the year 2020.
Whereas, the accident occurred on 09.03.2021.
No supportive documents are furnished to show that as on the date of accident, the petitioner was doing milk vending business.

Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence, this Court is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2021, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 17,000/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
26. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
27.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P7 and other medical records reveal that in the accident the petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1.Subdural hemorrhage.
2. Subarachoid hemorrhage.
3. Fracture of right parietal bone.
Tympanic and mastoid parts of right temporal bone.
The Doctor has opined that injury No.1 to 3 are grievous in nature.
Further, P.W.4 has also reiterated about the grievous injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident.

28. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
29.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
30.

The petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 09032021 and discharged on 15032021 in Hemavathi hospital and from Krishnaveni B.C vs Renukaiah P.H on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145936825/
6 16.03.2021 to 18.03.2021 in the THS Super speciality hospital.

31. Upon going through Ex.P10 and 11 i.e., the Discharge summaries shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 09032021 and discharged on 15032021 in Hemavathi hospital and from 16.03.2021 to 18.03.2021 in THS Superspeciality hospital i.e., for 10 days.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 10 days.
32. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.34,000/ under this head (@ Rs.17,000/ per month ).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
33.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
34. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical expenses.
He has produced 30 medical bills at Ex.P.12 amounting to Rs.53,067/ and 5 medical bills at Ex.P.28 amounting to Rs.14,522/.
I have gone through the medical bills.
The acceptable medical bills totally amounting to Rs.67,589/.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.67,600/ as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
35. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is unable to carry out his day to day activities.

36. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.Bhanu Prakash as P.W.4 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked OPD card and disability certificate at Ex.P.31 and Ex.P.32.
He assessed the whole body disability of the Petitioner at 69.77%.
PW.4 has reiterated the averments stated in the affidavit.
He has denied the suggestions putforth to him by the Learned Counsel for Petitioner.
In the crossexamination he admitted that he has not personally treated the Petitioner and he has examined the Petitioner on 05.12.2022 for the purpose of assessing the disability.

Further he admitted that wounds of the petitioner require conservative Krishnaveni B.C vs Renukaiah P.H on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145936825/
7 treatment.
Though the doctor who got examined as PW.4 assessed the whole body disability @ 69.77%
it is to be noted that the injured/petitioner appeared before this court and got examined himself as PW.1 and deposed regarding the alleged incident.
He also subjected for cross examination and has given rational answers during his cross examination.
If this factor is taken into consideration, this Tribunal is of the view that the disability assessed by PW.4 appears to be at the higher rate.

As such,
I am of the opinion that upon consideration of the injuries sustained by PW.1, if the disability is taken at the rate of 15% it would meet the ends of justice and equity.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 11.

With multiplier of 11, income of Rs. 17,000/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to her whole body at 15%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.3,36,600/ (Rs. 17,000/ x 12 =
2,04,000/, Rs.2,04,000/x 11 x 15/100 = 3,36,600/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,36,600/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
37.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 67,600/
5. Loss of income during the laid Rs. 34,000/ up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.3,36,600/ Total Rs.5,46,200/ Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.5,46,200/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

38. Issue No. 2 in MVC No.1673/2021 : As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
39. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown her age as 40 years.
She has produced her Aadhar card at Ex.P.10.
As per Aadhar card, the date of birth of the Petitioner is 0101 1979.
The accident has taken place on 09032021.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 42 years, and the same is to be taken for the purpose of assessment.

Krishnaveni B.C vs Renukaiah P.H on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145936825/
8 40.
It is to be noted here that, according to the petitioner, she had sustained grievous injuries.

But,
the medical record produced by the Petitioner herself, i.e., Ex.P.19 Wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.
1. Superficial abrasion over both knee joint and thigh 2. Superficial abrasion over left hand over dorsum 3.
Superficial abrasion over right forearm and elbow 4. Superficial abrasion over forehead.
The Doctor has opined that Injuries are simple in nature.
The Petitioner has produced Discharge summary at Ex.P.21 which shows that Petitioner was admitted on 09.03.2021 and discharged on 11.03.2021.
In order to prove the gravity of the injuries, the Petitioner is expected to produce documents.

But,
the documents produced by the Petitioner shows that she had sustained simple injuries.
The evidence shows, the Petitioner had admitted in the hospital for three days and incurred expenditure of Rs.1,00,000/ for her treatment and other expenses.

But, upon going through the medical bills,
i.e., Ex.P22 shows the total acceptable medical bills are amounting to Rs.7,661/.
It is not the case of the Petitioner that she has suffered from any permanent disability.

Admittedly,
the Petitioner is aged about 42 years.

In the absence of fracture or other physical disability and considering the simple injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for medical expenses, pain and sufferings, food and nourishment, this Tribunal is of the opinion that awarding global compensation of Rs.50,000/ would be just and proper.
41. Regarding Liability
: As already discussed above, in this case the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA04MW6914 was chargesheeted.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, Respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 2 in both petitions as "Partly in the Affirmative".
42. Issue No.3 in both cases : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner in MVC.1418/2021 against the Respondents No. 1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner in MVC No.1673/2021 against the Respondent No. 1 and 2 under Sec. 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

9

The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.1418/2021 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,46,200/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.

The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.1673/2021 is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondents in both the cases are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle in both cases, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner in MVC.1418/2021, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Epayment after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years.

On deposit of the Award amount and  interest by the Respondent No.2 in  MVC.1673/2021, since the same is meager one, the entire amount shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E Payment after her proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/ respectively in both cases.
Draw Award accordingly.
Keep the Original Judgment in  MVC.1418/2021 and the copy of the  Judgment in M.V.C. No.1673/2021.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
21. Though the Respondent No.2 had taken contention that the accident does not caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, it did not lead any evidence to substantiate its contentions.
Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Chargesheet against the driver of the offending car.
22. The oral and documentary evidence of P.W.1 and PW.2 and the materials available on record,
clearly shows that the said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the said accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and Petitioners in both the cases have sustained injuries.
In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 49 years.
The Petitioner has produced Aadhar card at Ex. P.9 to prove his age.
The accident took place on 09.03.2021.
Whereas, the accident occurred on 09.03.2021.
No supportive documents are furnished to show that as on the date of accident, the petitioner was doing milk vending business.
Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence, this Court is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2021, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 17,000/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
As such,
I am of the opinion that upon consideration of the injuries sustained by PW.1, if the disability is taken at the rate of 15% it would meet the ends of justice and equity.
In order to prove the gravity of the injuries, the Petitioner is expected to produce documents.
But,
the documents produced by the Petitioner shows that she had sustained simple injuries.
It is not the case of the Petitioner that she has suffered from any permanent disability.
In the absence of fracture or other physical disability and considering the simple injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for medical expenses, pain and sufferings, food and nourishment, this Tribunal is of the opinion that awarding global compensation of Rs.50,000/ would be just and proper.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.

42. Issue No.3 in both cases : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner in MVC.1418/2021 against the Respondents No. 1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner in MVC No.1673/2021 against the Respondent No. 1 and 2 under Sec. 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.1418/2021 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,46,200/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Petitioner in M.V.C. No.1673/2021 is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/ along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondents in both the cases are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle in both cases, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner in MVC.1418/2021, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Epayment after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years.
On deposit of the Award amount and  interest by the Respondent No.2 in  MVC.1673/2021, since the same is meager one, the entire amount shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E Payment after her proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/ respectively in both cases.
Draw Award accordingly.
